This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the appellant/ claimant for enhancement of compensation awarded in M.C.O.P. No. 402 of 2016, dated 05.06.2020 on the file of the Chief Rajendran vs Prakash on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163644823/
1
Judicial Magistrate, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Namakkal.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Namakkal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred herein according to their litigative status before the Tribunal.

3. The case of the claimant is that on 17.01.2016 at about 4:00PM, he was riding a TVS XL Super two wheeler bearing Registration no. TN-28-AS-3235 at Andagalur Gate on Thiruchengode to Rasipuram Main road, while he reached near Government Thiruvalluvar Arts College, a Hyndai I 10 Car bearing Registration No. TN-54-7101 belongs to the first respondent came in the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the claimant's two wheeler, thereby causing grievous injuries to the claimant.

A criminal case was also registered against the driver of the Hyndai I 10 Car bearing Registration No. TN-54-7101 in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Cr.No.31/2016 under section 279, 337 of I.P.C. on the file of the Rasipuram Police Station.
Due to injuries sustained, the claimant has come forward with this claim petition seeking compensation for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- along with interest under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
4. The first respondent is the owner of the Hyndai I 10 Car bearing Registration No. TN-54-7101 has not contested the claim and remained ex-parte.

The second respondent - insurance company has filed a counter and contended that the accident was happened only due to the rash and negligence on the part of the claimant and the first respondent's driver is not responsible for the accident.

The insurance company has relied on the Motor vehicles inspection report for their claim and disputed that the claimant has no valid driving licence to drive the two wheeler and also contended that the compensation claimed under various heads are on the higher side, hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, P.W.1 and P.W.2 were examined and Exs.P.1 to P.13 and Ex.C1 were marked.
On the side of the respondent, no witnesses were examined and no exhibits were marked.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

Based on the evidence placed on record, the Tribunal in point no.1, has held that the accident was happened due to negligence on the part of the claimant as well as the first respondent's driver, hence fixed the contributory negligence in the ratio of 15:85 on claimant and driver of the first respondent vehicle.

In point no.3, the Tribunal has quantified and granted compensation for a sum of Rs.8,86,800/- after deducting contributory negligence of 15% on the part of the claimant along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till the date of realization.
In point no.4, the Tribunal has fixed the liability on the second respondent - insurance company to indemnify the owner of the first respondent car and to pay the compensation to the claimant.

7. Aggrieved over the quantum of compensation, the claimant has come forward with this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation and no challenge was made on the liability of contributory negligence fixed on the claimant as well as the driver of the first respondent.

Rajendran vs Prakash on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163644823/
2 8.

The learned counsel appearing for the claimant has submitted that the claimant has suffered multiple fractures on the head and he has been https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis properly diagonised and fractures sustained revealed that the claimant has suffered greater pain but the Tribunal has not appreciated the same.

Hence, no proper compensation was awarded by the Tribunal for the disability sustained and the compensation awarded under other heads is also on the lower side, hence prays to enhance the compensation.

9. The learned counsel for the insurance company has submitted that the Tribunal after assessing the disability certificate marked in Ex.C.1, has come to a conclusion that the claimant has not sustained any functional permanent disability and prays to confirm the same.

10. Heard the submissions made on both sides and perused the materials placed on record:
11.
The claimant has marked the discharge summaries of the Manipal Hospital, Salem, which are marked as Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.6.

The Ex.P.5 discharge summary shows that injuries have been investigated by CT and MRT and the above injuries shows that the claimant has sustained severe head injury, Left Global Rupture with vitreal tissue prolapse, CSF https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis rhinorrhea and fracture on the Multiple Facial Bone on the Mandible and Maxilla and MCL teat Right knee Joint.
The Ex.P.6 discharge summary shows that the claimant has undergone left secondary orbital implant placement for left socket reconstruction under GA.

In the MRT scan,
there was a small sized contusion in bilateral basifrontal cortex is noted.

These injuries shows that the claimant have sustained severe injuries on head due to multiple fractures and considering the same, the Tribunal has granted Rs.70,000/- under the head pain and suffering.
This Court is of the view that the same is on the lower side and inclined to modify the same to Rs.1,00,000/-.

12. The Ex.C.1, disability report issued by the medical board shows the claimant has sustained disability of 37% and the same is fixed by the Tribunal as permanent disability and not as permanent functional disability, hence adopted percentage method and granted compensation of Rs.3,000/- per percentage of disability.

It is also the case of the claimant that he is a mason by profession and on perusal of the Ex.C.1, it is clearly recorded that the claimant apart from the head injury, has a vision impairment on the left eye and right knee mild instability.

Considering the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis nature of injuries sustained by the claimant on the head and vision impairment, this Court is of the view that the injured cannot continue his earlier avocation of mason, since it involves physical work.

13. The Hon'ble Apex Court judgment in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar [2011 ACJ 1] has given a guidelines as well as illustration for fixing the disability and granting compensation under the head loss of earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar [2011 ACJ 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court is of the view that it is a fit case to treat the disability sustained by the claimant as a functional permanent disability, which results in loss of his earning capacity.

The claimant has suffered Left Global Rupture with vitreal tissue prolapse, CSF rhinorrhea and fracture on the Multiple Facial Bone on the Mandible and Maxilla and MCL teat Right knee Joint supports the case of the claimant that he sustained multiple fracture and injuries all over his body.
These injuries thus resulted in various complications more particularly vision impairment and right leg instability.

Due to injuries sustained, he has now been prevented from doing his earlier avocation Rajendran vs Prakash on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163644823/
3 of mason.
This Court is of the view that the loss of earning capacity has to be fixed as 15%.
Accordingly, this Court is inclined to grant compensation under the head loss of earning capacity by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis adopting multiplier method.

On perusal of the Ex.P.13, aadhaar card of the claimant, it shows that his date of birth is 23.08.1970 and the accident was taken place in the year 2016, hence, the age of the claimant is 46 years at the time of occurrence and following the dictum laid in the judgment in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in [2009 ACJ 1298 SC : 2009 (6) SCC 121], the multiplier is fixed as '13' by considering the age of the claimant, hence the loss of income due to his disability is assessed as follows:
Total Annual income (12,000 x 12) = Rs.1,44,000/- Loss of income due to 15%
disability = Rs.21,600/- The Multiplier adopted is 13, hence (21,600 x 13)=
Rs.2,80,800/-
14.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in [2009 ACJ 1298 SC : 2009 (6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., reported in [2020 SSCR 299 : 2020 ACJ 2159], the claimant is also entitled for future prospectus and this Court awards 25% as future prospectus on the loss of income due to his disability, which was not awarded by the Tribunal, hence this Court is inclined to grant the same as follows:
Loss of income due to 15% disability = Rs.2,80,800/- Future prospectus @ (25% of 2,80,800/-) = Rs.70,200/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 15.

entities.text: Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., reported in [2020 SSCR 299 : 2020 ACJ 2159]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since this Court has awarded compensation under the head loss of earning capacity,
compensation awarded under the head loss of income during treatment period is hereby modified as loss of amentities.
Whereas the compensation awarded under other heads are concerned, the Tribunal has awarded a just compensation, hence this Court is inclined to confirm the same.

16. Accordingly, the award passed by the Tribunal under various heads are hereby modified as follows:

1 . Loss of pain and 70,000/- 1,00,000/
 suffering  2. Towards permanent 1,11,000/- 2,80,800/
 disability/ Loss of  earning capacity

3. Medical expenses 7,92,300/- 7,92,300/
 4. loss of earnings during 45,000/- 45,000/-
 treatment period/ 
 modified as loss of  amentities  5. Transport expenses 15,000/- 15,000/-
Rajendran vs Prakash on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163644823/
4  6. Extra Nourishment 10,000/- 10,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  S. Description Amount Amount   No awarded by awarded by  Tribunal this Cour  (Rs) (Rs)
7 . Loss of future --- 70,200  propectus
Total 10,43,300/- 13,13,30  Deduction with respect 1,56,495/- 1,96,99  to 15% Contributory  negligence  Total Compensation 8,86,800/- 11,16,30  (round off)

15. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.8,86,800/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.11,16,305/- [Rupees Eleven Lakh Sixteen Thousand Three Hundred and Five only] together along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of Claim Petition till the date of deposit, excluding the default period, if any.

The second respondent - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount awarded by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.402 of 2016 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Namakkal.

The Tribunal shall disburse the amount now awarded by this Court by directly giving credit to the Savings Bank Account of the claimant.
Since this Court has enhanced the compensation, the appellant/claimant is directed to pay the necessary Court fee, if any, on the enhanced compensation.
There shall be no order as to costs in the present appeal.
